hints: Think about the target that ends first. Its shot must be somewhere inside it — where inside it would hit the most other targets?
Greedy by right end: sort targets by right, fire at the right end of the first un-hit target, and that shot covers every target whose left ≤ that position.

1. Sort targets by right end.
  2. shots = 1, pos = right end of the first target.
  3. For each next target: if its left > pos, it is not hit — shots++, pos = its right end.
  4. Return shots.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Try every candidate shot position (all endpoints) in every combination until all targets are covered.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Sort by right end and fire at the right end of each target not yet destroyed.

explain: Sample 1 sorted by right: [1,5],[4,8],[9,10],[10,14]. Fire at 5: [4,8] has left 4 ≤ 5, so it is hit too. [9,10] has left 9 > 5, so fire again at 10, which also hits [10,14] (left 10 ≤ 10). Total 2 shots. Shooting at the earliest right end is as far right as you can go while still hitting that target, so it catches the most others. Since endpoints are inclusive, use left > pos to decide a new shot; compare with Integer.compare to avoid overflow on big values.
recognize: Fewest points that stab every interval → sort by end and place each point at the earliest uncovered end.
